title: Underrated but not perfect
body:
I found this app through Structured and the combo is your final battle :D I have pro in both apps. It’s fairly priced and I appreciate that they have a yearly subscription only and not these annoying monthly ones. Pro: works well, I love the customization for different apps and reasonings to why you need to open the app. Also love the analysis when you open one sec telling you how much time you’ve saved on other apps. I also love the explicit content blocker. The App Switching is an important feature too. Con: The Layout of the app can be a little difficult to understand at first. Not very inviting. It’s also difficult to find the shortcut video tutorial at first. The main con however is that onesec isn’t suitable for all apps yet. I have games I need to limit that apple shortcuts just won’t allow me to because of the settings in that specific app itself - not bc of one sec. Very annoying however and there needs to be a solution for working around this.
Overall a fantastic app needed by many more people on many more devices! Great Job!

title: Die App ist Klasse - der Support nicht so.
body:
Ich habe vor zwei Jahren als Geschenk einen Lifelong Lizenz erhalten da der In App Kauf im Zuge des Indie App Santa Specials nicht funktioniert hat. Diese hat jetzt aus unerfindlichen Gründen nicht mehr funktioniert. Vom Support bekam ich nur die Nachricht, dass es solche Codes nicht mehr gibt und Codes nur noch ein Jahr gültig sind. 

Ich finde die App selbst wirklich herausragend, aber es hinterlässt einen faden Beigeschmack wenn man eine Lifelong Lizenz bekommt, die dann aber doch irgendwann nicht mehr funktioniert. Über Geschenke beschwert man sich natürlich nicht, aber bitte nicht sagen die Lizenz gilt für immer, wenn es nicht stimmt. :( 

Ich habe mir die den Einzelkauf jetzt gegönnt weil ich von der App überzeugt bin, aber wenn ich das gewusst hätte, hätte ich das lieber damals schon gemacht, als es noch günstiger war.

title: intentional app switching behind a paywall.
body:

What annoys me most is that ‘intentional app switching’ is a toggle you can only turn on if you pay? 
One of the most infuriating things, because if I am having a conversation or doing something on the app and are switching between, everytime I go back into it I have to wait that one second again.
Intentional app switching shouldn’t be behind a paywall, it just makes the app so inconvenient and takes away from all of the positives, and I’ll likely delete it because of this. Don’t get me wrong, the app and the idea of it is great, but this one feature makes the whole thing so annoying.

title: Only content blocker that has ever worked for me.
body:
The way this app, and it’s desktop and web versions, has improved my quality of life is impossible to understate. Ran it for one week on Facebook, and then immediately purchased the full version. I expected it to be one of those things that I stay on top of for a week or so, then fall off the bandwagon. 2 months in and I’m still going strong, and noticing that I don’t miss a thing.

$25? Pro is the biggest change the littlest amount of money has ever made in my life.

Previous content blockers, I’d uninstall, or work my way around. This is the only one that has effectively worked. I have never considered deleting it once. It does the complete opposite of all the social media, attention grabbing tactics, giving you the space to slow down and actually think.

I feel so much more in control of my own mind, so much happier. Thank you to the developer for helping me get that back. I highly recommend this app to anyone who struggles with distractions on their phone.

title: Changed my life
body:
Where do I even begin? This app brought a change to my life that was desperately needed. After struggling mentally for years and drowning myself in mindless scrolling my screen time was anywhere from 6-14 hours a day. I realised that I was spending almost half my life on something that I would only remember for a few minutes afterwards. It was taking time away from more meaningful things like family, study and hobbies that I actually enjoyed doing and brought something to look forward to each day. 

Even though it has only been a couple days after downloading this app, it has taken my time on my phone to only 1-2 hours a day (which is mostly just keeping in touch with friends, family and school). I have had time to take up crocheting which I thoroughly enjoy and feel that I am able to concentrate more at university. My mental health has already improved, I feel more connected socially, and am being more productive than I ever have been. I find it amazing how just a quick 10 second break can make you question whether or not you really need to be on social media. 

To the makers of this app; thank you. You have brought a change desperately needed in a time where so many people are detached from reality and have made my life so much more fulfilling in mere days. Everyone should download one sec!

title: Very good, some improvements would make it much more usable.
body:
It works very well, my feedback for improvement would be:

• Enable user-customised colours on the breathing animation, as some of the presets aren’t very aesthetically pleasing.

• The one-sec automation is triggered every time the app is “opened”, meaning even a momentary change in apps, or opening the App Switcher screen on iOS, causes the animation to trigger again when returning. Is it possible to configure a time delay (eg 5 minutes of inactivity) before triggering the one-sec shortcut and animation??

• Related issue to the second suggestion — Apple’s iOS displays a tiny app switching button in the top left corner of the current app, intended to allow iPhone users to return quickly to their previously used app. Unfortunately some social media apps (Reddit) make it is easy to accidentally trigger this by mistake and exit the active app, causing a one-sec animation when returning. Unsure how this could be resolved, but it’s quite annoying and warrants some attention?

Otherwise, thank you for creating this app, it functions pretty much as advertised.

title: Great concept, great execution
body: Alleged “Extra long intervention” for settings lock being a literal standardized 10 seconds really ruins this app for me. My brain doesn’t have the executive function to maintain one sec’s interventions active with such a puny intervention for the settings lock. I love, love, love this app, but I have to speak out about this, cause this app is fundamental for me, but also ultimately worthless because I always eventually bypass it through the scheduled block setting. I mean, it doesn’t even make any sense to have a 10 second “extra-long” intervention for one sec’s settings while it simultaneously being only the third longest option in the order of 7 possible options (3s, 6s, 10s, 20s, 40s, 60s and 120s). Please, please, please, please add the option to increase the settings lock intervention time. It’s only logical. This isn’t a minor request, at least for me, as the lack of it literally makes the app meaningless for me.

title: Best app I’ve ever bought
body:
I have for months been resigning myself to the fact that I probably just need to get a dumb phone to curb social media and YouTube’s impact on my life and time. Then this app came into my awareness and changed everything. Truly, if you’re worried about screen time, this is the app for you. 

The setup instructions are easy to follow and I can’t believe what a difference it’s made in the last month or so since I bought it. I went from hours of scrolling to…maybe half an hour a day maximum? The interventions are just inconvenient and effective enough to really work, and having to write my intention for using social media every time is a game changer.  At night, I put it on a reoccurring strict mode and it’s also revolutionized my sleep. No more getting sucked down late night YouTube rabbit holes. 

It is exactly what I’ve been wanting and I’m so grateful I found it 🙏 truly, if you’re also struggling, get this app. It’s more than worth your money for the full version

title: Just try it!
body:
I was skeptical but, the app was free so I gave it a shot. After an adjustment period where I kept being SUPER annoyed & changing settings constantly, it high key started to work. In fact it worked so well I went from wasting at my peak 8 hours of my life on an app I felt trapped on to deleting Instagram after nearly 12 years of almost daily use. I’ve now re-downloaded Instagram with little to no restrictions placed on it & I still don’t want to use it anymore.

Yes it took awhile, for me it was about 9 months. I upgraded to premium maybe 4 months in to utilize the “re-interventions” feature, this isn’t a quick fix but, trust me the constant interruptions are training your brain no matter how you respond to them. I even found what many are saying is a “glitch” where the intervention takes 5 seconds to pop-up letting you catch a glimpse of the app you’re trying to open was good because usually, the dumb reel I suffered through the intervention to see wasn’t worth it & I started hating social media for that! 

I also appreciate that the updates they post explain bug fixes in plain language & the instructions for how to set up interventions are similar. The app has no forced ads that are bothersome, except for their paywall and it doesn’t limit the usefulness of the app it just kind of limits how many tools you can utilize & is slightly annoying to exit out of which I found to be pretty reasonable. I was even offered a discount when I did finally get premium, which was great. Its refreshing to finally have an app that seems like it’s trying to actually provide a helpful service first & foremost, instead of focusing mostly on being profitable to the detriment of the user. 

So yeah thanks to the whole app team ya’ll are doing a great thing (& your marketing clearly isn’t too shabby either), so far I have regained about 4.8 weeks of my life thanks to you & the power of annoyance.

title: I hate how well this works.
body:
I’ve only been using this app for about a week, and yet I’ve already noticed that the time spent on my target app is greatly reduced. It really does make you stop and think about what’s really important to you in the moment. And the forced breathing exercise is so annoying (as it’s supposed to be) that I’m noticing I’m not even trying to open the app half as often as I normally would. Also, being told how many times you’ve tried to open the app in a 24 hour period really puts things in to perspective. My compulsive scrolling habits were so much worse than I thought they were, but I’m seeing improvement already! Watching the number of attempts go down over time is quite satisfying.

If you do need to switch away from the app for a moment it is annoying in the free version to have to go through the exercise again, but the intentional app switching feature in pro helps. Of course, if you don’t actually have a reason to need to come back right away, making it annoying on purpose is good too.

title: Good for the impatient or busy, ineffective if you’re willing to wait
body:
I started using onesec via their Firefox extension, which lets you configure as many sites as you want, and I use the free version of onesec to block the Safari extension as a whole, as I deleted all my social media apps a while ago and access them via browser. 

I have my browser extension set to 30 seconds, displaying a version of the “Litany Against Fear” quote edited to be about scrolling, and my phone app is configured to 20 seconds. To a lesser being, this long wait time may be enough to starve out your app-opening impulse. I am, however, a persistence hunter of the desire to waste time. onesec is perfect for me not in that it redirects me away from my impulse to use Twitter or other social media — all it does is let me waste 20-30 seconds (more like 30-40, the breathing animation lasts a small percentage longer than you set it) more than I would otherwise have on social media. 

This isn’t an issue exclusive to onesec, and I assume this app is very useful if you have a brain that wants to cooperate with you to reduce your social media usage. Unfortunately, I’m too accustomed to circumventing roadblocks between me and my next tweet, so I will have to look elsewhere for a weapon strong enough for me.

title: Legitimately Life Changing
body: One sec says it's saved me hours in a few weeks, but it only counts preventing an open as saving 3 minutes. With how I was spending time on my app vices before the app, I know I've gotten back LITERAL DAYS of my precious mortal life. Premium is more than worth it and I appreciate a non-subscription model. I do wish very much that I could set multiple time spans for the "back to reality" reminders. 3 minutes is fine for instagram, but way too short for YouTube, for example. And once I ignore the first reminder, there's nothing else ever until I leave the app again on my own. If I could have reminders at 3, 5, 10 and 30 minutes, for example, the accountability would continue, and it would seem like a simple add to the app's functionality. Even better would be different reminder times for different apps, but just being able to pick more than one time span would be spectacular and help with the last issue I'm dealing with in app usage.

title: Love the app But waiting on premium because…
body:
Love this app, 9/10 times when i’m opening instagram without meaning too (out of habit/boredom,etc) I don’t want to sit through the 6 seconds and close it. Awesome!!! Does what it’s supposed to do. 

However the one fault I have noticed (and not really a problem with the app but more with me) and the reason I’m not buying premium yet; is that when I do have the app open (either from that 1/10 time where I did sit through, Or I had opened the app with the intent to respond to a message etc), I think subconsciously I will spend longer on the app then I need to because I already have it open and I know how long it takes to open so I don’t wanna have to wait and reopen it later so instead I just stay on it? So when I it stops me from opening it works, but once I have it open I think I stay on longer (kinda like revenge scrolling).

Again an issue with me not the app! If there was some way to mitigate this issue I would definitely be purchasing premium! Maybe the an option to have the app force close every few minutes? Or when you turn off your phone the app makes you redo the wait screen time? I’m not sure! 

But a fantastic app thank you:)

title: Curbing Addiction - as long as you pay
body:

We can only hope Apple integrated an idea like this internally for a faster and free solution

title: One that works if you set it up correctly
body:
I’ve tried a lot of screen time apps, and OneSec is the one that actually changed my habits. The key feature for me is scheduled blocking: you can lock apps completely during set time windows. My setup is no social media in the morning, open during lunch from 12 to 1 pm, and open again in the evening from 6 to 8 pm. Outside those windows, they’re simply off.

The effect has been huge. My screen time has dropped dramatically because I no longer fall into the habit of opening apps reflexively. Instead, I use them deliberately, at times I’ve chosen. I don’t wreck my dopamine system first thing in the morning anymore, and I don’t lose focus to long Instagram sessions when I’m in a flow state during the day.

It takes a bit of thought to set up the schedules so they fit your day, but once you do, it works remarkably well. Highly recommended if you want to take back control of your attention.

For example I’ll start a block session and it starts and simply didn’t block any app, I can still open the apps, but I can’t cancel the block of course, because it’s a strict block (this happens on my phone too. Die App läuft weitestgehend lokal auf dem Handy, Serverkosten dürften also minimal sein. Es sei denn die Entwickler verhandeln/ haushalten schrecklich.

title: Tolle Idee, eher "schlechte" Umsetzung
body:
Das Prinzip ist wunderbar. Ich habe auch direkt ein Jahresabo abgeschlossen um dieses Projekt zu unterstützen.

Leider ist die Funktionsweise echt nicht so geil. Vor allem WhatsApp ist für mich persönlich ein Problem. Ich öffne ständig die App, einfach weil sich die muscle memory da so abgebildet hat.
In erster Linie geht es mir darum einfach schnell auf alle Chats zu gucken. Danach schließe ich die App meistens wieder. 
Nun habe ich mit Hilfe des Tutorials eine Automation erstellt um mich daran zu hindern. Sie funktioniert auch. Nur leider verzögert, wodurch ich die App trotzdem kurz sehe, bevor eine Intervention angezeigt wird. Der Energiesparmodus ist deaktiviert und auch sonst beeinträchtigt nichts die Leistung meines Handys. Die App hat alle angeforderten und benötigten Berechtigungen und Zugriffe von mir erhalten. 

Das ist sehr schade, auch vom Support kommt seit ewigkeiten keine Antwort auf meine Anfrage. Ich verwende ein Iphone 15 Pro Max

title: Guter Ansatz mit mangelnder Ausführung
body: One Sec hat eine noble Idee, braucht wegen iOS Einschränkungen aber die Shortcuts App und Bildschirmzeit als Krücke für die eigentlichen Funktionen. Jede einzelne App Automation muss separat eingerichtet werden, bei iPad+iPhone dann auch mal zwei. Das ist nicht so schlimm wie es klingt, denn viele Apps lassen sich schlichtweg nicht blockieren, da One Sec sie nicht zur Rücknavigation in seiner Liste führt. Die wenigen Funktionen, die das unübersichtlich gestaltete One Sec Pro selbst bietet, wie zB. das Empfehlen alternativer Apps oder die Selbstreflexion, warum man eine App nutzen möchte, sind lieblos umgesetzt, wobei die Selbstreflexionen innerhalb der App ohne Konsequenzen bleiben.  Der Preis von 35€ oder das Abonnement sind für dieses simple „Pro“ Produkt nicht gerechtfertigt. Glücklicherweise kann man die App für eine Woche nutzen und anschließend selbst entscheiden, ob man diesen Preis zahlen möchte oder die meisten dieser Features einfach selbst via Shortcuts und Bildschirmzeit einrichtet. Nach ausgiebiger Selbstreflexion und reichliche Atemzüge später komme ich zu dem Schluss, dass mich diese App mehr Zeit kostet, als sie mir zurück gibt. Ich bin in der Studie scheinbar im Randbereich der bell curve.

title: Wie man sich selbst wieder kontrollieren kann
body:
Unbewusstes und ungewolltes öffnen bzw. nutzen von Youtube, TikTok, Instagramm und co. endlich unterbinden.

In langweiligen Momenten öffneten meine Hände schon automatisiert irgendwelche Apps nur um einen kurzen Dopamin Kick zu bekommen. 
Über das elendige Gefühl und den Frust über sich selbst und die eigene Disziplin kennt wohl ein jeder von uns.

Durch unheimlich vielfältig Einsetzbare und individuell Anpassbare Möglichkeiten kann ich endlich wieder mein eigenes Konsumverhalten lenken.

Der Jahresbeitrag von 6€ ist kaum der Rede wert.
Alleine die ersten Tage nach Installation und der Funktion, eine gesunde Alternative (bei mir Babbel) öffnen zu lassen ist mir wesentlich mehr wert.

Danke für diese wundervolle App und all die nun sinnvoll genutzte Zeit. 

PS: Eine MUSS für alle Eltern, die ihren Kindern einen gesunden Medienkonsum nahebringen wollen und sie vor den Suchtmechanismen der Unterhaltungsindustrie schützen wollen.

(Ja, leider arbeiten diese Konzerne mit den besten Psychologen zusammen und wenden die gleichen Methoden wie die Glücksspielindustrie oder der Dealer von nebenan an)

2. Beispiel : ich will auf Instagram und nur kurz auf meine Dms klicken um zusehen ob es sich überhaupt lohnt, und muss aktuell immer  erstmal warten bis ich nachsehen kann… 

Das verfälscht auf der einen Seite weniger die Öffnungsversuche der Nutzer ( durch verzweifeltes Versuchen ganz schnell noch auf die DMs zu kommen auf einmal +10 Öffnungen 😂 )  und würde denn Stress den das warten  auf die Freigabe auslösen kann, in Situationen wie solchen, deutlich verringern.

title: Beste App um Zeit am Handy zu reduzieren
body:

Social Media Apps durch eine Intervention darüber nachzudenken, ob man jetzt wirklich auf Social Media chillen will, oder ob man seine Zeit nicht vielleicht produktiver nutzten könnte, nein sie ermöglicht es einem auch ganze Apps zu bestimmten Zeiten zu blocken, Tagebuch zu führen, schlägt gesunde Alternativen vor, usw.
Die App hat praktisch unendlich viele Einstellungsmöglichkeiten, das Support-Team ist extrem hilfsbereit und das Design der App ist sehr ansprechend.
Mir hat die App (in Kombination mit einigen Einstellungen der Bildschirmzeit) geholfen, meine Social-Media Nutzung mindestens zu halbieren und so weniger Zeit am Handy zu verbringen!

title: Die App hat meine Psyche gerettet
body:
Vielen Dank für diese App! Ich leide an AD(H)S und hatte die schlechte Angewohnheit mir meine Dopaminkicks von diversen Social Media Plattformen zu holen. Seit ich one sec nutze konnte ich meinen Social Media Konsum drastisch senken und bin mittlerweile so weit, dass ich manche gar nicht mehr nutze. Das war unterstützend zu einer Therapie auch sehr wichtig um aus einer schweren Depression herauszukommen.

Social Media und Smartphones sind meiner Meinung nach  Krankheiten, welche unseren Dopaminhaushalt volkommen kaputt machen. Die Ursachen und Auswirkungen lassen sich unter anderem in Anna Lemkes Buch “Dopamine Nation” nachlesen.

Vielen Dank nochmal für die gewonnene Lebenszeit!

Ich verstehe es nicht – früher zahlte man für eine solche App ein paar Euro und konnte sie Jahre nutzen. Diese App kostet rund 30 Euro oder man zahlt jährlich 15€ im Abo. Wenn man das nur mit jeder dritten Apps da draußen so machen würde, die man auf seinem Smartphone installiert hat, würde jeder gut 200€/Monat zahlen, nur um Apps auf seinem Smartphone zu nutzen. Natürlich macht das keiner. Aber wundern müssen sich die Entwickler dann auch nicht, warum die Anzahl an Käufen nicht höher ausfällt.

title: Coole App mit ein paar Macken
body:
Tolle App und auch bereits im kostenlosen Umfang vergleichsweise brauchbar. Ich wäre grundsätzlich auch bereit für die App zu bezahlen, finde den Preis abee für den überschaubaren Funktionsumfang recht überzogen.

Leider ist die App noch an ein paar Stellen recht verbuggt. So lässt sich die „Re-Interventionsabfrage“ nicht mehr deaktivieren nachdem man sie einmal aktiviert hat und hier hilft nur eine Neuinstallation der App.

Auch kann man die Intervention in der kostenlosen Variante entfernen, hat dann aber keine Möglichkeit mehr diese hinzuzufügen oder zu konfigurieren. Auch hier hilft nur eine Neuinstallation.

Auch die Zeitangaben sind für mein Empfinden deutlich kürzer als die Tatsächlichen Wartezeiten bis man die App starten kann. Mir persönlich reicht hier auch eine kurze Intervention, um zu entscheiden ob ich die App wirklich öffnen will. 

Die App Wechsel Funktion ist sehr vorteilhaft, ebenso die Push Nachricht nach einer voreingestellten Zeit. Nervig nur wenn man beim Countdown das Multitasking Menu öffnet oder ähnliches und der Countdown abbricht. 

Ansonsten erfüllt die App aber ihren Zweck.

title: Super App! Hat mir sehr geholfen
body:
Ich finde die App super, sie hat mir definitiv dabei geholfen meinen Social Media Konsum besser unter Kontrolle zu bekommen und auch allgemein produktiver bei der Arbeit zu sein.

Ich hätte jedoch noch 2 Verbesserungswünsche, damit die App wirklich eine 10/10 wird:

1: Das man eine Option hat, um die Atemübungen für einen bestimmten Zeitraum zu deaktivieren (z.B. 30min, 1 Stunde…)

Das hat den Hintergrund, da ich auch mindestens einmal täglich in meinen Social Medias beruflich rein muss und mich dort die Atemübungen etwas nerven, da ich ja bewusst für den Zeitraum in die Apps möchte, um zu arbeiten.

2: Das man bei der „Block Session“ mehrere Optionen mit verschiedenen hinterlegten Apps hat.

Ich möchte zum Beispiel manchmal bewusst nicht auf Social Medias und starte dann die block session. Ich habe aber auch teils Phasen, in denen ich gerne WhatsApp mit dazu blockiert haben möchte.

Daher wäre es sehr cool, wenn es dort in Zukunft ein feature gäbe, mit dem man bestimmte „Block Sessions“ abspeichern könnte.

All in all aber auch jetzt schon eine Top App 👍🏽

Was jedoch wirklich hilft, ist diese App. Ich versinke nicht mehr stundenlang in For-you-pages und erwische mich, dank one sec regelmäßig dabei, wie ich versuche, Instagram zu öffnen ohne wirklich darüber nachzudenken. Die App ist übersichtlich, sieht schön aus, hat gar keine Werbung und die Pro-Version ist ziemlich billig. Die Entwickler wollen hier offensichtlich nicht möglichst viel Geld machen sondern den Umgang der Menschen mit ihrer Technologie verbessern.

Leider habe ich gemerkt, dass die App auf meinem Iphone 12 mini super viel Akku zieht und dass das Iphone häufig sehr heiß wird, wenn sich one sec aktiviert. Da meine Akkulaufzeit nicht mehr die Beste ist, musste ich die App schlussendlich doch wieder deinstallieren.

title: Tolle App!
body:
Endlich mal eine App, die es richtig macht! 
Ich habe jetzt schon mehrere Apps ausprobiert, um das Verlangen nach Apps wie Instagram, Facebook, Tik Tok und co. zu dezimieren. Allen voran natürlich die interne Bildschirmzeit-Beschränkung von Apple. Keine hatte bisher einen so guten Ansatz wie diese App. Es macht in meinen Augen viel mehr Sinn schon vor der Nutzung einer App anzusetzen. Eine Nutzung nicht zu bestrafen, sondern inne zu halten und die eigene Entscheidung nochmal in den Fokus zu rücken, ist eine fantastische Idee.
Abgesehen davon ist diese App gut durchdacht und umgeht systematische Hürden, indem sie sich die Kurzbefehle App zur Hilfe nimmt und Tipps zur Nutzung gibt, die auch mal funktionieren.

Da bekommt man das Gefühl, dass z.B. die interne Bildschirmzeit Beschränkung von Apple gar nicht wirklich will, dass man bestimmte Apps weniger nutzt…

title: UNGLAUBLICH GUT !!!
body:
Ich bewerte zum ersten Mal eine App, das sagt schon mal einiges aus! 😂 aber diese App ist so so gut!
Bevor ich one sec benutzt habe um meinen Instagram Konsum in den Griff zu bekommen, habe ich Instagram 7-9 Std in der Woche benutzt, also durchschnittlich 1 Std+ am Tag.
IN DER ERSTEN WOCHE mit one sec, hat sich die Zeit AUF 1,5 STD reduziert!!! das war so krank und hat mir so die Augen geöffnet.
Vorallem die Anzeige wie oft man versucht hat die App zu öffnen, lässt einen wirklich staunen. Außerdem bemerkt durch die Animation man nun wirklich bewusst dass man die so oft unbewusst App öffnet! Wirklich unglaublich.
In der zweiten Woche hat sich meine Instagram-Zeit auf unter 1 Std in der ganzen Woche gesenkt! Es geht also wirklich schnell und man wird sich schnell bewusst wie viel schöner es ist ohne durchgehend auf Instagram zu sein!

Ich kann es wirklich jedem empfehlen!!!

body:

Ich hab bereits nach kurzer zeit für 9,99 das jahresabo gekauft und denke das ist sehr gut investiertes geld für mich.
Ein kleiner Punkt wäre noch schön:
Für die Blockierungen sollte der zähler wie oft man die app öffnen wollte dringend mitzählen. Ich hab zb für arbeitstage/homeoffice komplett geblockt und trotzdem erwische ich mich ständig dass ich es versuchen will. title: Kostenlose Version
body:
Die kostenlose Version hat mich überzeugt, sobald ich etwas Geld übrig habe, werd ich mir die Pro Version holen.

Aber:
Kann ich die Pro Version dann per Family Sharing mit meiner kleinen Schwester teilen?

Oder muss man die pro Gerät kaufen?

Super fände ich, wenn man den Appbutton und auch die insgesamt Oberfläche benutzerdefiniert farblich gestalten könnte:)

Außerdem wäre es auch cool, sich eigene Nachrichten ans Ende der „Atemauszeit“ zu schreiben, z.B. dass bei Instagram immer auftaucht:
„Willst du dein soziales Bedürfnis nicht lieber durch einen Anruf bei xy stillen?“

Oder was even benutzerdefinierte passt.

Wäre sowas möglich?

Toll wäre auch eine Weiterleitung zu einer anderen Achtsamkeitsübung, so dass es die zusätzlich zu der Möglichkeit die besagte App zu öffnen oder es zu lassen noch die Möglichkeit gibt „mache stattdessen eine Minute Achtsamkeitstraining“.

Es gibt ja viele tolle Atem und Achtsamkeitsübungen. Mehr Varianz wäre da toll.

Aber Overall super Idee und schöne App.

title: Funktioniert aber überteuert
body:

Ein Preis von 10€ pro Jahr ist für die Funktionalität (von der man das meiste nicht braucht) allerdings zu
viel verlangt. Dabei geht es nicht um „nicht leisten können“, ich bin einfach nicht bereit für so eine simple App so viel zu bezahlen, und zu abonnieren.

Die free version erlaubt one sec nur für eine App einzurichten. Wenn man zwischen Apps kurz wechselt wird auch immer wieder one sec getriggert, was supernervig ist und wovon man nur erlöst wird wenn man zahlt. 

Typische unmoralische deutsche Gier.

Es ist wahrscheinlich nicht möglich, aber gewünscht hätte ich mir, dass wenn man die persönlichen Konfigurationen an einem Gerät gemacht hat es auch auf die anderen Geräte übertragen kann.
 
Ist eigentlich geplant one sec auch für die Macs/MacBooks anzubieten?

Einziger persönlicher Kritikpunkt (da ich extrem abgedriftet bin in SocialMedia etc.) ist, dass es bei der Fokus Variante die Möglichkeit gibt diese auch unterbrechen zu können. Klar, man muss diese nicht anwählen und es gibt bestimmt Menschen die sich einigermaßen unter Kontrolle haben, aber für süchtig ist es dennoch eine unglaublich Versuchung. Es ist am Anfang immer ein Kampf gewesen diese Option nicht zu wählen. Mittlerweile ist meine Routine beim Aufstehen als erstes den Fokus für den Tag, für die Stunde wo ich arbeiten soll, einzuschalten, denn am Morgen bin ich noch willentlich am stärksten. Safari ist auch in dieser Zeit geblockt 😢, ich denke näher komme ich dem kalten Entzug nicht …

Noch mal einen großen Dank an die Entwickler!!!

Es ist wichtig zu beachten, dass es eine Pro Version per in-App Kauf gibt. Monatlich für 4,99€, jährlich für 19,99€ und LifeTime für 39,99€. title: Super Idee, große Einschränkungen in der Free Version
body:
Ich finde die App super - Idee und Umsetzung sind an sich wirklich toll. Ich kann auch verstehen, dass man eine Free Version so gestaltet, dass es Anreize gibt, zur Paid Version zu wechseln. Aber in der Free Version von dieser App ist Twitter für mich auch beim bewussten, achtsamen Öffnen der App kaum nutzbar.
Hauptproblem: wenn ich Tweets sharen will, geht das nicht komplett „in-app“ sondern bspw. WhatsApp wird zum Teilen geöffnet. 
Dadurch wird nach dem sharen jedes Mal wieder die Durchatmen-Automation ausgelöst. Das ist dann einfach ein zu großes Usability-Problem. 
Um dies zu umgehen bräuchte es die App-Wechsel-Funktion aus der Paid-Version. 
Generell ist für mich das schnelle Wechseln zwischen Apps eine zu essenzielle Funktion, die für mich in die Free Version gehört.

title: Wirkt gut, kleine Probleme
body:
Ich mag die Idee, daher als Versuch installiert.
Einige kleine Dinge, die etwas stören: wenn ich nach einer Sekunde auf "Nicht öffnen" klicke, lande ich in der One-Sec-App und nicht auf dem Home-Bildschirm. Da komme ich dann nur wieder raus, wenn ich auf den Home-Button klicke. Der "Zurück"-Pfeil oben leitet zurück zu Twitter und die ganze Automation geht von vorne los. Die Beschwerde klingt vielleicht kleinlich aber der Ablauf ist mir direkt zwei Mal so widerfahren. Eine direkt Leitung auf den Home-Bildschirm wäre cooler.
Hinzu kommt, dass die Einrichtung für nicht so Technik-affine schwieriger sein könnte, ich selbst kenne mich recht gut aus und ich hab zwar nur 5 Minuten gebraucht, aber es war jetzt nicht unbedingt intuitiv (Was vor allem an der Apple-Kurzbefehle-App liegt). Ich glaube z.B. meine Mutter würde die Einrichtung nicht hinbekommen.
Und dann noch ein Hinweis: ich probiere die App jetzt erstmal aus und setze die Bewertung dann ggf nochmal hoch. Das Problem ist, dass ich bereits beim Zweiten öffnen der App nach einer Bewertung gefragt wurde, da habe ich gerade mal die blanke Funktionalität ausgetestet, kann aber noch nichts zur Wirksamkeit sagen. Vielleicht könnte man die Store-Aufforderung zur Bewertung etwas später setzen.
Wie gesagt, es sind nur Kleinigkeiten und meine Hinweise konstruktiv gemeint. So weit ich es bisher einschätzen kann (nach dreimaligem Öffnen halt) macht die App einen guten Eindruck.

Esta es la segunda vez que me descargo esta app. La primera vez fue hace muchos años, entraba a Twitter de manera inconsciente y pasaba HORAS ahí metida. En un tweet me encontré con el desarrollador de esta app, que hablaba de ella y la probé. Mi vida cambió drásticamente, con el tiempo me di cuenta de que la app me estaba generando ansiedad (Twitter), me desintoxiqué y la elimine. Llevo 4 años sin entrar a Twitter, ya no lo tengo siquiera. Ahora lo necesito de nuevo con Instagram, no sé qué emociones encontraré esta vez, pero se 100% seguro que esta app es lo que necesito y va a funcionar.
Mil gracias, desarrollador, por hacer esta aplicación. La has mejorado mucho! Y gracias también por devolverme el “tiempo”, es lo más valioso que tenemos ❤️

title: Funciona muy bien a un módico precio
body:
La verdad que me ha funcionado mucho y he pasado de estar 6h al día con el teléfono a 3h.
Si que es verdad q hay q pagar 14€ AL AÑO. Pero a mí me mereció mucho la pena.

Pros:
- Vas a bajar el consumo de la aplicación o página web 100% 
- Precio razonable si lo comparas con el exceso de horas que pasas usando la aplicación. 
- Bastante cómodo e intuitivo.
- Puedes compartir la app en otros dispositivos. (Pagando un poco más) 

Contras: 
- La única pega q le encuentro son los 14€ al año. 

Tiene cosas a mejorar y pequeños fallos, pero es muy buena app 

Cosas a mejorar o ideas para añadir:
-Las intervenciones. Al entrar a la app restringida son siempre las mismas, creo q estaría bien que hubiera un modo aleatorio o algo así y poder variar la intervención. 

-Notificaciones de uso de la app. Te notifica aunque ya hayas salido de la aplicación, y es un poco molesto. (Aunque se puede desactivar)

- Creo q en las “intervenciones” al exceder el tiempo de uso, podrían añadir  la opción de penalizaciones a la hora de “esperar a abrir la app”. Es decir, q si excedes el  tiempo de uso seleccionado por ti previamente, vas a estar 20s de espera como intervención.

title: Mala
body:
Tienes que crear numerosas automatizaciones para cada App, para cuando se abra, cuando se cierra... Connlo sencillo que sería que utilizase la API de iOS Screen Time. Las configuraciones no son nada claras para el usuario y tiene muchos fallos.
Además, estaría bien que tuviese una opción de Quick Open para cuando necesitamos abrir rápidamente Instagram por ejemplo para responder a 1 mensaje, estableciendo un límite de Re-Intervención de 1 minuto aproximado.
La característica de Re-Intervención es muy molesta, podría dejar que configuremos un tiempo por defecto en vez de preguntarnos cada vez que abrimos la app.

En resumen, la App ha empeorado mucho, se ha vuelto complicada, lenta, poco útil, y además es muy cara.

title: Sigh
body:
Could be good! More payment period options for pro could be fine. It’s either nothing or a year? Is there really no in between? 0,99 per month would be stellar, and you’d still get more than your year’s worth of money if people decided to stay. And they would… if it worked. 

The app is DEEPLY flawed. I set up my shortcut according to instructions and instead of getting a breathing notification when opening my app, I was stuck in an endless instruction screen limbo. No matter how many times I disabled it from the Settings or clicked “done” after reading the instructions… it would just open that page all over again. Im way more stressed now and should’ve just gone to Instagram to begin with. 

Just make a note saying “breathe” and make a shortcut to that. Works better, is free, and doesn’t drain your energy.

title: Incroyable, quelques ajustements à faire
body: Cette application est absolument génial, car elle permet de se rendre compte lorsque nous traînons sur les réseaux de manière même pas consciente. Dans les transports en commun, dans une file d’attente, ou n’importe quand dans la journée on se rend compte du nombre de fois où nous ouvrons les réseaux. Cette application nous permet de nous rendre compte que nous sommes en train de l’ouvrir et donc de revenir à la réalité. Cependant, il y a juste une petite amélioration à faire., c’est de pouvoir personnaliser le temps gagné à chaque fois que l’on évite d’aller sur une appli . Actuellement c’est automatiquement trois minutes, mais ça serait chouette de pouvoir modifier ses données, par le temps moyen réel que l’on gagne en évitant une appli, car c’est très rarement trois minutes, en général lorsqu’on va traîner sur Instagram par exemple c’est plutôt 15, 20 minutes, voire une heure. on se rendrait donc beaucoup plus compte de l’impact que du temps gagné grâce à cette appli.

title: Meilleurs app de développement de soi avec « Structured »
body:
Développeurs honnête, version Pro accessible à tous (financièrement), et efficient si un minimum de volonté et de motivation intrinsèque. 
Features simples mais efficace.

Contrairement aux autres applications, une vrai envie d’aider chacun, plutôt que du marketing uniquement avec pour seul but d’avoir les abonnements mensuels, les plus chère. 
Une offre d’achat en une seule fois est même disponible, malgré que je considère, l’abonnement à l’année plus rentable, on est pas obliger de payer mensuellement et ça ça me donne encore espoir en ce monde. 

Une offre étudiante qui fait plaisir, si vous avez un petit budget, mais une grande envie de s’améliorer. (Et de ne plus être aliéner par les réseaux sociaux, cette application vous permet uniquement que de réfléchir, mais n’oublions pas que c’est la chose la plus formidable qui existe, et c’est ce qu’il nous manque aujourd’hui à tous).

title: Passée de 4h+ par jour sur Insta à 1h max
body:
Je note très peu les apps mais là franchement je peux que recommander 

J’ai testé mille milliards dapps de productivité et franchement celle ci est une des meilleures, parce qu’elle désamorce totalement l’utilisation machinale des apps. 

Je suis super addict à Insta je pouvais passer parfois 12h par jour dessus en vacances et en semaine surtout ça m’empêchais de faire ce qui me plaisait vraiment. Le système tout simple de la respiration est vraiment rédhibitoire et décourageant et permet de se poser « one sec » avant d’ouvrir ses réseaux. 

La partie gratuite est excellente et je vous conseille d’appairer avec l’app Structured pour avoir un rappel de vos activités à faire à la place des réseaux inutiles. Merci!

title: Barnabullement séduis !
body:
En effet,
Hier matin j’ai installé cette application… sans prétention particulière… 
Mais au bout de 45 semaines 1 jour et 34 minutes je me rends compte qu’elle a changé ma vie. 
Désormais je ne me laisses plus attraper par ce piège du système que sont les réseaux sociaux et je n’ai plus aucun ami (même pas un). 
Je me divertis des plaisirs de la vie en dehors des écrans tels que… je n’ai pas d’exemple en l’occurrence mais bon. Mais mes journées sont bien occupées je vous assure ! Bref revenons à l’essentiel, j’en conclus que cette application est une bénédiction pour ceux qui n’ont pas envie des distractions de nos jours 
Point positif : je parle beaucoup à Angélique, ma tortue domestique et à Freudon mon phasme de compagnie (Henri étant décédé, soit dit en passant) Repose en paix mon ami.

title: A must-have
body:
I can't remember the last time I felt so strongly compelled to write a positive review.
I don't consider myself to have a problem with doom scrolling or screentime for the most part, but I have one digital vice - YouTube. I have premium and it's probably my favourite entertainment platform.
I noticed that my Screentime was creeping up over time into numbers that I wasn't comfortable with.
With all other apps I was wasting time with and knew they werent bringing me any value, I simply deleted them, cold turkey, about a year ago and have no regrets. But YouTube felt different, I do get genuine value from it whether that be entertainment, educational or practical. The problem was the volume and lack of intentionality.
Although it's early days I can whole heartedly say that one-sec has completely changed the dynamic and feels like the perfect solution I was missing all this time. In just one week my Screentime reduced by 45% while feeling like I wasn't even trying. Through a combination of blocking schedules and interventions, the frequency and duration I spend on YT has dropped dramatically and I can feel better habits forming already.
Often you really do only need the intervention, but I do like having the scheduled block features to stop me from checking work apps when I'm off the clock.
As others point out, the setup is a bit unconventional and less straightforward than some of the alternatives. But it is absolutely worth it, and the instructions are still clear enough.
More than happy to pay the modest annual fee for such a high-impact and well thought out experience.

author: danjw96

title: My second time reviewing - milestone achieved
body:
This app has changed my life, and got me my most valuable asset back: 

My time.

Since May 2023, I have saved 4.3 weeks of SCREEN TIME on Instagram, and another couple weeks across multiple different social media’s.

Across the board, I have saved 1.4 MONTHS of screen time. Just think about that for onesec (excuse the pun) 

Overall ‘app opening’ preventions currently sit at 19,701. 

In fact, my milestone has now been achieved:

The blockers were genuinely so annoying to bypass, I started to get frustrated and it clearly conditioned my brain to resent the app in question that was being blocked, in this case, Instagram. I have now uninstalled Instagram, and I can say confidently that I am much happier without it. 

You actually realise after you don’t have some of these apps that their presence in your life is meaningless, and they literally give you zero value.

The only social media app I could justify using is “X”, which I still have yet to even use, but it’s a platform of free speech and uncensored content so that you can make your own informed decisions about the world without being reliant on mainstream media. Again, just make sure you have the blockers in place & re-interventions (stops you from doomscrolling / getting you into rabbit holes for hours) 

Nevertheless, it’s actually quite scary to think that some of us can’t live without social media. It used to be me. 

The truth is, whether or not you have social media on your phone, the world keeps spinning. It’s up to you to decide what you do with your time as it spins. 

I trust you’ll make the smart decision that I did back in May last year. Install the app and get your time back. 
 
Massive thank you to the developers, hopefully one day I’ll meet you and treat you all to a drink. 

Alex
United Kingdom 
24/09/2024

body: Instagram reels to me can feel like getting sucked into a black hole where i lose my grip on reality and can’t stop scrolling. Having one sec interventions makes me aware of my surroundings every 5 minutes meaning i can enjoy the funny videos on Instagram without missing out on my day. I use apple’s screen time feature as well to limit Instagram to an hour per day and I have someone else who knows the screen time password. This means I can only do ‘one more minute’ once when the time runs out. I feel like I am in control of my time now. I like the features one sec has especially the new scrolling wheel to choose the amount of time you want before an intervention which is way more purposeful than before when you hit a button to choose the time. This app is very helpful to my life.

author: Adarsh.123

title: Great alternative to Screen Time!
body:
I have previously used Screen Time to help me not look at my phone as much, but have run into frustrations with its all or nothing approach. One Sec is the middle ground I’ve been looking for as it provides lots of ways to discourage me from opening apps. Making it annoying (in a beneficial way) without making it utterly impossible is the best way for me I think.

The only things it’s missing for me are

1) the ability to hide the settings menu behind a long intervention to prevent the temptation of changing settings to get around the limits
2) some way to auto generate the shortcuts needed to make the app function

Great work!

For a few months now, that feature is broken, even though I’ve reset my shortcuts app and updated everything. I always need to redo the exercises when I leave and come back to an app. 

Also I now get an annoying additional pop up every time I open or close an app asking “what’s your intention” then a list of apps for me to choose from. It’s just another irritating thing that is unnecessary. I can’t find any way to turn it off. 

I emailed support before the new year and had an initial response asking for more detail but then heard nothing. 

I’m still using it but it’s kinda broken right now.

title: Really really good
body:
This app is really really amazing and I’m glad it exists. It is already helping me to reduce certain compulsions to open certain apps, and prevents me from staying on each app too long.

There are some bugs or potential features though:

- “I don’t want to open this app” could pop out a bit earlier or maybe immediately so we can cancel right away. I know we can just navigate away from the app though but this would be a nice feature.
- PIP intentions don’t seem to show up for apps, only for Safari. Not sure why, am I doing something wrong or is this a known bug?
- video previews of the interventions (or an in-app simulation of the intervention)
- ensure that all interventions support features like Healthy alternatives. Eg I think that the circle tracing one doesn’t support this feature of Healthy alternatives. Along with this, some documentation such as a matrix of interventions and features, with checks/crosses, would be nice.
- morning countdown could work for other apps than just the delayed apps. Eg I don’t want to make it hard for me to use Telegram or WhatsApp but I may want to stop myself from using them in the morning when I wake up (I have friends in the East so they send me messages while I’m asleep so there is lots of temptation to reply to them when I wake up). But they shouldn’t be intervened any other time of the day.

title: A change I’d love to see being implemented!
body:
I’ve been using this app for about a month now and even bought an yearly subscription. Love the app and what is strives to achieve, but I have only a single gripe with it, a small change I’d like to see made which would make this even more functional in my opinion. 

Users like me have chosen longer pauses like 10-60 seconds when opening apps so what I noticed was both, the option to opt out of the app and continue the app come into view after the said time passes, which makes it a tougher decision to opt out of it immediately. 

So what I mean to say is please place the button of exiting the app on top of the timer overlay and let the `continue to app’ button remain below the overlay of the timer. Please do consider this as I think people would more often click to exit than wait for both the options to appear and give themselves an excuse to just continue instead. Thank you!

title: 🔝 App
body:
It’s a must have. Setting it up might be a little tricky if you’re not familiar with shortcuts, but tutorial are already in-app to help dealing with it. 

I wanted to ask two things though: personally, i like the intervention more than the blocking, so I was wondering if it were possible to have per-app personalised intervention, just like the blocking schedule. 

The other thing is: I personally like to schedule everything I have to do during the day in Structured, but some tasks don’t need an intervention, so a function to ignore certain tasks would be useful, in my opinion. 

Nevertheless, great app, I really mean it, best money I have ever spent on an app. 
Keep up the good work 👍🏼

title: Incredible
body:
I tried this app out on a whim and now all my friends use it too. Sick of being chronically online and this app helped break a lot of habits. Delaying instead of preventing is far more effective since it just makes opening twitter, reddit, or instagram that much more inconvenient. I bought a year of the full version and haven’t looked back. My screen time over the past 3 weeks has plummeted.

I would appreciate a bit more customization with some apps outside of social media. Like preventing me opening Slack outside of work hours, or similar. But as it is, this app is still very effective and packs a whole lot of features, and the price is extremely affordable. I’m sick of apps which offer wellbeing improvements charging an arm and a leg, and this app is a breath of fresh air.

I wish their web browser extension for PC had a few more features, but thats a minor nitpick. 

Incredible app, incredible value.

title: An app that I need and would recommend 👍🏻
body:
At first I was just going to try it out because I have tried a couple of apps by now to help control my impulsiveness. But most of them didn’t really appeal to me and some are just way out of my budget. 

I just wanna say that this app has it all: 

(1) blocking certain apps you want to block at a specific time, 

(2) the automatic interventions whenever you open the app you are trying to avoid or lessen the usage,

(3) the countdown/timer that will make you see how much time you’re spending scrolling through social media apps (while also tracking your real intention for using it) and many more *chef’s kiss* it’s just perfect! 🤩 

These are just the features that I love! ❤️ 

I already feel like a different person because it saves me time and from doom scrolling. From 5-7 hours of screen time, I was able to lessen it to 30 mins max a day. This app helps me to be aware and to stay focused 💪🏻 Talk about effectiveness 💯 but I must say that a part of it also comes from discipline and with the intention of trying something out to help change the bad habit. 

For first time users like me, it can be challenging to set it up at first if you’re not used to setting up automations, but the steps are provided in the app so you won’t get lost 😊 

It’s the fairest of them all and at an affordable price 👏🏻 I’m a current Structured Pro user and I’m taking advantage of the discounted offer. 
Kudos to the developer/s. This app is wonderful and a great help!

title: Lyckas stoppa scrollandet på riktigt
body:
L-Ä-T-T en av dom bästa apparna på AppStore 👌

Till skillnad från Apples värdelösa "screen time" (som går att låsa upp närsom) så spärrar den här appen det du valt på riktigt.

Fattar inte riktigt recensionerna som klagat, ja den var lite svår att sätta upp förut (verkar finnas några lättare sätt nu) men att den var krångligare att sätta upp är ju också det som gjorde att man inte orkade ta bort spärrarna vid minsta infall heller för då behövde man ju göra om allt igen 🙃👌

Bästa med appen:
* man måste vänta några sekunder innan apparna du lagt till öppnas, så att man kommer av sig lite med att ta upp mobilen och bara börja scrolla

* kan lägga till påminnelse när man varit inne och scrollat på samma app i exv 10 minuter

* bäst: kan ange skärmtid per dag per app - som inte går att bryta med bara en enkel kod

* kan lägga till varning som kommer upp exv 5 min innan tiden går ut när man är inne och scrollar per app

Finns massa andra delar också men det är dom 👆 jag iaf använder mest.
Och ang. priset så fattar jag inte hur nån kan klaga på det; alla timmar man sparar med den här appen gör att man går plus med priset på nolltid.

Nu blev det här en kanske överdrivet positiv review 😅 men gick in på sidan för att kolla en annan grej och började läsa några negativa recensioner från folk som ganska tydligt inte fattar vad appen är till för så behövde skriva av mig 🙃

Grym app, rekommenderas 100%.

- - -

For the developers; thanks for a great app and if you could somehow add support for restricting sites via the Brave browser as well that would be amazing ✨✨

title: Amazing for attention management!
body:
I've tried other apps that do the same core thing (block addictive apps for a few seconds to help reduce the dopamine hit you get from opening the apps) - and this is the absolute best one. You can tell the developer cares about his users through being extremely thoughtful in the usability. I have three favourite functions: 
- Sometimes I need to switch to another app to copy and paste something or if I'm clicking a link (the link opens in browser) - you can set up one sec to allow you to go back to the original app again without having to go through another intervention. (This feature itself makes me continue to use this app - I have deleted other similar apps because the interventions were too annoying. Yes I want to be annoyed and that is the purpose but I don't want to be annoyed to the point of non-usability.)
- I also love the doom-scrolling intervention which allows me to continue using social media but forces me to go through another intervention and actively reminds me of how long I have been using it. (Didn't realise how useful this was until I set it up - after clicking 3 or 4x of 15 mins, I realised I had been mindlessly scrolling social media for too long.)
- Schedule time periods when certain apps are blocked. I set mine to my sleeping and productive hours.

I don't use this function but URLs are blockable too, not just apps. 

Set up was easy. The basic features are great and the pro features are absolutely worth it if you are serious about being in control of your life instead of letting apps dictate it for you.

title: For developer: missing a lot, please read everything
body:
Correct me if Im misunderstanding anything. This is coming from a developer of multiple years

first of all let’s start off with how almost every single feature is paid. I know that the you developers need the payment to continue working on it well, but some features that are behind a paywall are GENUINELY necessities that shouldn’t cost a dollar. For example you can’t even intervention block more than a single app without getting the subscription, and if you tested the app well you would know that most people need to block more than 1 app. Surprise surprise if TikTok is blocked I’ll just switch to Insta.

second I shouldn’t have to create a shortcuts automation every time I add an app to one sec. other focus apps allow you to block multiple apps in seconds. “linking” an app twice for each block/intervention is a bit redundant, it should just let me choose what apps i wanna block from a list. 

then there’s the fact there’s very little securing of your blocks unless you pay. it’s TOO easy to just delete the Shortcuts Automation to stop the app blocking forever, or just use the TikTok.com instead of the TikTok app (cause strict blocking is paid too…)

It’s also REALLY annoying how a bug fix was turned into a Pro feature (Intentional App Switching). Normally if you got timed out from an app, you would close the app for 5 minutes, take a break, and come back after 5 minutes. Well with one sec you have to wait the full 5 minutes INSIDE the app to be able to use it again, or you’ll have to wait for the timeout to expire every, single time you reopen the app. Only way to fix this? get pro which is stupid 

The last straw was when the stupid intervention feature wasn’t working properly at all. I needed to use YouTube for an emergency but every time I went through the intervention YouTube was still blocked. Don’t make so many features paid if the basic ones aren’t even working properly.

Developer, correct me if I misunderstood anything but in my opinion it’s not the most effective and a bit cash grabby. there are other focus apps like Opal with the same features for free

title: Changed my life! Would recommend one big change though
body:
I LOVE one sec! I've been using it for at least a couple of years now. The combination of using One Sec and deleting the instagram app has basically changed my life. The best features are: 
1. Being able to set time frame blocks for certain apps and websites (so helpful for not scrolling during work hours or late at night!)
2. Being able to set a timer for how many minutes you'd like to spend in the app before another intervention
3. Just making my distracting apps and websites less of a favorable activity (aka more annoying bc I keep getting interrupted!)

I would only make one big change to improve this app. Let's use Facebook for example. When you click on Facebook, it immediately runs OneSec and starts an animation such as the screen going dark for several seconds. This is designed to slow you down and help you consider clearly whether you actually want to be opening that app right now. It's meant to prevent mindlessly opening up apps. When the animation is finished,  it asks you if you really want to open facebook. Well, you've already waited the several seconds for the animation- you may as well open it! You open facebook. 

If onesec asked me if I wanted to open it BEFORE the intervention animation started, that would be a game changer. That way it would be a trade: you have to pay to open this app- you can only open it if you wait several boring seconds first. Then if you click yes to continue to the intervention, and then the intervention finishes, it still asks you what your reason for opening the app is and how many minutes you want to spend on there before another intervention. 

Mane this could be a setting you ca toggle on and off, so if anyone doesn't like that system they can opt out. THEN the app would be perfect. What do we think?

title: Strong blocking, but missing real accountability
body:
This app does a good job enforcing Screen Time limits, but it falls short as an accountability tool.

Like most Screen Time apps, it relies on three mechanisms:
	•	app time limits
	•	unlocks / temporary access
	•	scheduled blocks

The problem is that following or breaking these rules isn’t meaningfully tracked. Users can:
	•	repeatedly use unlocks
	•	change limits or schedules after enforcement starts
	•	revoke Screen Time permissions and re-enable later

…without any persistent history or consequence inside the app. That makes it easy to undermine your own rules quietly, which defeats the purpose for serious users.

What would make this a 5-star app:
	•	an accountability history (unlock usage, schedule adherence, rule changes)
	•	logging Screen Time permission revocations/restores
	•	an integrity metric (did I keep my word or not)
	•	brief, optional reflection prompts at key moments (before unlocks, after rule changes)
	•	weekly summaries focused on accountability, not just usage minutes
	•	a place to define and revisit why you’re limiting apps, so behavior change is internal, not just enforced

Blocking alone changes behavior temporarily.
Accountability, integrity tracking, and reflection change it long-term.

If these additions were made, this would easily be a 5-star app.

title: Really helpful and super customizable
body:
I have been using one sec for about a year or two now, and I originally used it primarily for the main “Take a deep breath” to give myself an unskippable cutscene before opening Instagram and YouTube. It works really well and it’s definitely annoying but that’s the point and it has assuredly helped break a lot of my brainrot cycles.

I’m giving it a review now because I recently started also using the app blocking feature, which allows you to set up a schedule such that certain apps can be blocked at certain times. I used to run late every morning because I would just doomscroll for way too long after waking up, but I set up a schedule to block all social media and games on my phone in the morning hours. It works really well and you can also set it up so that it’s literally impossible to turn off while it’s active, which is a feature I needed. 

The app offers a paid subscription for $19.99 a year with lots of other cool features, but the best part is that the features I just described are completely free! It’s helped me immensely in not getting lost in the sauce on my phone and I am very grateful.

title: Great option if you’re addicted to social media but too addicted to delete it yet!
body:
To be honest, I’m not really sure why I downloaded this app. I don’t even have social media. I thought perhaps it could aid me with keeping off of my YouTube app, which it did— only for me to watch YouTube on my TV instead LOL. 

I can see this being a good app for people who do have social media and need guilt-tripped into not doomscrolling. For me, this app just made me realize that I’m addicted to YouTube so I ordered about 20 books and will be deleting YouTube from my phone when they arrive. I think the “time saved” part of the app is inaccurate because I always spend more than 5 minutes on YouTube. I think I’d like to see some type of more realistic “summary” feature in this app. So at the end of the week when I get my screen time report from Apple I also get a notification from this app saying how much time I actually saved myself based on how long I usually spend on apps. 

Overall, though, this is super creative and the most effective way I’ve seen so far at keeping people from wasting time on their social media. The setup is confusing though, even for a young adult like me. Don’t think that can be worked around unfortunately. 

If I didn’t have the self-control that I already have not to have social media in the first place, I would definitely keep this app and pay for the subscription. I will likely be recommending it to people who ask for tips to stay off their phone.

title: Good app except for one thing
body:
Everything about this app is great, but having to pay for intentional app switching is crazy.

The fact that it’s there shows that the app can tell when you only want to leave something for a second, which means people who don’t pay will:
- naturally get used to skipping the reminder when it’s intentionally put in your face for no reason
- stop caring about the number of times they’ve opened an app because the number is at least doubled by this alone

All of the other premium features make sense, but this just feels like the devs don’t want the app to work for free long term. 

Other than that, it’s pretty nice.

title: Very grateful I bought premium on One Sec
body: Crazy how these large corporations made social media apps so powerful that I'll subconsciously go on Instagram and snapchat without even thinking about it. Whenever there was pause in a video game, nothing going on in the moment in life, or I'm bored, I'd naturally pick up my phone and by default go to Instagram with 0 purpose. After I downloaded one sec and bought premium it made my unconscious habit conscious. It makes me ask myself in my head, "is there anything I absolutely need to do on this app?" If the answer is no, I get off. The habit has subsided too because my mind associates checking social media as one sec popping up. So grateful I got this because I'm a lot more mindful and in the moment than I was before and I'm a lot happier and less irritable. I highly recommend you get this app because if your someone like me who doesn't wanna delete their socials, this makes you in control of your decision to go on these high dopamine apps rather than the corporation being in control of you.

title: Great app, but…
body: This is a very clever application that does precisely what it’s advertised to. It requires a form of intervention before opening an app of your choice, and this is highly customizable. There are lots of interventions to choose from, and how long you want them to be. You can also have it choose a random exercise for you, and it supports website blocking as well, which is nice. You can also set up a bedtime schedule where it blocks all apps and websites. It provides an informative dashboard detailing approximately how much time you saved. However, I really can’t get behind the modern era of subscription based apps. Especially for the lifetime license costing a whopping FIFTY dollars, and SEVENTY for a “family plan”. I don’t have any problem supporting independent developers and paying for software, but I personally feel like this is overpriced for what it does. Most of it is just relying on the iOS shortcuts functionality anyway, and all the app is doing is showing a pretty GUI and recording the time. You could replicate something similar in shortcuts (although not entirely, like website blocking for instance.) If you don’t mind the cost, go for it, but I would probably pay $15 maximum for a lifetime license, not $50. Especially considering many people using this are likely college students.

title: Great idea, but not well executed
body:
This app has honestly helped me curb my Instagram usage so much! I didn’t realize just how often I’ve been opening the app out of almost subconscious habit, but having this tool has helped me realize that I don’t have a good reason and I’m losing a lot of life I’d rather live.

They have a few other features, but the main one I downloaded the app for - the intervention - has to be set up one app at a time (so won’t block new games), and and worse yet, you can only set up interventions for a limited list of common entertainment apps. If you’re getting stuck on anything but the most popular games and social medias, this app can’t help.

Additionally, the app itself is confusing and difficult to navigate. All the possible features and integrations are in one big list, and it’s usually unclear what each thing does without a lot of experimentation. Having the main features highlighted with “enhancing features” as sub-parts, or having a tutorial that walks through all the main things you can do with the app, would be a lot easier.

author: Brin Ann

title: A great app that shows great promise
body:
I’m a student who has been struggling with procrastination for as long as I can remember. My phone, through social media and video games, has often been my source of that. I’ve tried other screen time apps in a desperate attempt to fix my problem, but all of them are easy to bypass and default back to wasting time. I was afraid that I would never be able to break the cycle. 

One Sec is the only program that forces you to reflect. And I mean, really, it forces you to reflect on yourself before you open the app that you designed. There’s nothing fancy about it - no bells and whistles like the other apps. That’s because change doesn’t come with bells and whistles, it comes from within. I’ve been using One Sec for only a day and I’ve managed to drop my average screen time about an hour and a half. It’s incredible, and I’m really giddy about how much I’ve been able to improve myself in only a day.

That being said, the downside of One Sec is that it doesn’t have any bells and whistles. You have to manually implement the shortcuts for all of the apps you want to block, and that is the meat and potatoes of this app - you don’t get much else that significantly helps you stop overusing apps. On top of that, the dashboard (overview) page of the app has very little content besides the list of apps that you blocked by hand and how much time you’ve saved through using One Sec (which seems inaccurate as I tend to spend a lot more time than three minutes every time I clicked on an app). 

But overall, this app is a great program that can help you beat overuse. More content and programs are sure to come as this app is just beginning, and I really look forward to it. I think that there are a lot of great things that can happen with this app, such as more content being added to the overview page (overall screen time, usage trend graphs, times you’ve continued to use the app despite the One Sec timer, etc) and making it easier to block apps. I’m very happy with One Sec and would recommend it to anyone looking to make a change for the better.

title: Wow. If everyone had this app, we’d be a better world.
body:

title: What Screen Time should be.
body:
The barebones version of this app is more than enough to genuinely make an impact on your screen time. Apple's integrated Screen Time feature isn't a realistic way to rework our additions to certain apps. The one minute feature often times isnt enough, and the 15 minute feature allows you to get sucked back into the content, putting you in an endless loop of "remind me in 15 minutes" until it's been hours. One Sec not only forces you to take a moment to make sure that you truly should be using the app, but with the free re-intervention feature, it's far more effective than Apple's own Screen Time. 

I can't recommend this app enough. It is truly made with people in mind, and the free features are more than enough to make a tangible difference in your life.

title: Useless.
body:
I’m so annoyed. I was really hoping I could use this app to curb my spending. Unfortunately, it’s useless at best and infuriating to use at worst.

Not only are the directions to set up blocking for websites basically useless (I had to Google and find answers on Reddit to figure out how to actually add websites to one sec’s block list), they also don’t even work. Even if you enable the one sec safari extension, somehow figure out you’re supposed to go to each individual website and tap on the extension button to block that website, and manage to create a block list, it simply will not work.

One sec blocked only one website for me, and the button it presented me to go back to the one sec app did not work. So I was not able to complete the breathing exercise. The app didn’t even recognize that it had blocked the website. Simply refreshing the website let me back in. After that, the blocking didn’t work at all, for that or for any website that I had put on my block list. What on earth is the point of a blocking app that doesn’t actually block anything?

Thank god I canceled before my free trial was up. It would have been a huge waste of my money on a useless app that does nothing when it comes to one of its most advertised features. If you’re looking to block websites, this app is basically a scam (because blocking websites is a premium-only feature). Stay away. I wish I could give zero stars.

title: Worked Great, Until It Didn’t
body:
I’ve been using this app (pro version) for months. It’s been great to help stop late night doom scrolling. Took a while to set up & get working properly for me, a big hurdle for ADHD brains, but worth it. 

Until suddenly it was telling me that “You cannot use [app name] because it is restricted.” Keep in mind that I ONLY have interventions set up for three apps from midnight-8:00am. 

Didn’t matter what time of day/night, I could not access ANY of those three apps. I managed to somehow figure out a fix for one, but for the life of me could not get it to work for the others. I turned off every thing I could find, eventually had to just completely delete the app as I needed access to event info ASAP. 

Now I’ll need to go and do the entire set up process again & even though it WAS helpful, this hurdle is one I dread facing again & not sure if I will. Paying up front for a year subscription was a mistake & I absolutely HATE this model of revenue.

title: I am over it 👎
body: I have loved this app since I began using it 6 months ago. It even inspired me to purchase my cousin an iPhone, knowing that I would be able to restrict their screen time and break the dopamine-induced doom scrolling that social media and games can oftentimes induce. When I was going to sign up for the family plan, I saw the price had increased from $25 to $40. For reference, the individual plan is $20. Honestly, if I only intended to add one additional user to the subscription, what incentive is there in not receiving a discount? Look at it this way: 2x individual plans = $40; 2x users on family plan = $40. What's the difference? This is really shortsighted and selfish of the developer, in my opinion, and it makes me want to not even renew the individual subscription. $40 is too much. The app is good and well thought out, but it isn't actually providing that grand of a solution to justify that price, even for multiple users. $25 actually motivated me to add users to the app, given it was only a $5 increase from what I was paying. Doubling the price only frustrates me and makes me want to protest the developer's greed, and it shows that their intent isn't to actually provide a solution and make that accessible to more people, but to squeeze every dollar from their user base. What a careless decision towards users. I'll be deleting the app.

These days no one can pay for an app with one simple fee; instead, app developers greedily want you to pay them month after month for an app that tells you to take a break from using your phone. I’d be totally willing to pay a one time fee because I hate subscription services. But if you’re not going to pay anything to them, the app is unusable because you’re only blocking one app, which defeats the whole purpose of having multiple target apps. 1 star

author: Brittfurreal

title: Brilliant
body:
This app is brilliant. I have it on all my iOS devices. I feel like most screen time reducing apps come and go, as half baked ideas put together over a weekend. This one is different. It feels as put together, or even more so, than Apple’s own screen time controls. It’s obvious the creator of this app made this for themselves as it applies to users’ real uses very well. I’m someone who uses various ways to make my devices more “dumb” or minimal. I mix this with feed blockers, screen time settings, greyscale, and not having social media apps on my phone. This is a very important piece of my already pretty elaborate puzzle.

This app can probably do more than I can grasp right now. I just use it to slow load apps and make them get progressively slower overtime. As my dopamine rush gets slower every time I wait for an app to load, I could just delete this app out of frustration. But I don’t. I feel like a kid knowing maybe it’s best if only mom can open the cookie jar. I also use the app for app blocking which is super cool. 

My only request is if I could set a timer for app blocking. What I mean: set timer and in 25 minutes all apps on the list will be blocked. That way maybe when I need or want to go down the rabbit hole, there is going to be a hard cutoff upcoming that I can’t stop. Otherwise I’ll just willingly not stop and go down a binge, which I unfortunately too often do.

title: Reduced Instagram from 1hr/day to 1hr/week
body:
Instagram used to be my default time wasting app, to the point where I would go on it without even really being conscious of what I was doing. I tried screentime and the setting on Instagram to notify me if I spent more than ten minutes on the app, but neither really worked. 

Within a couple weeks of downloading one sec, my usage went way down. One day my sister mentioned something she had posted the day before, and I realized I hadn’t seen it because I hadn’t been on Instagram for over 24 hours. And I’ve found that when I do go on it, I spend less time on it than I used to - it’s just not that interesting anymore. I’m so glad I downloaded this app as it was exactly what I needed!

PS if you are a student get the student discount!

title: Lifesaver of a time-saver
body:
I’ve been trying a few things to make my phone more annoying to use, or helpful when I do, and not a boredom eraser. One Sec is something that I wish I had years ago. I finally feel like I have the opportunity to fill my downtime with something other than my phone screen! My adhd makes all of this harder than it might otherwise be, but with a little help from this app (and a lot of work on myself), I’ve started journaling, meditating, budgeting better, doing more real-world projects around the house… the Structured integration helps with that too. By the way, I’m not sure why people are complaining about the price. $20 for a whole year is practically nothing.

Something I’d like to be able to do with the app is set a time limit on how long you can use a particular app before the interventions start. That way (if I’m good) I don’t have to wait for the intervention while I’m out at the store and trying to look something up before buying it, for example.

title: Manipulative design choices try to annoy you into paying
body: I really want to love this app. In the free version, any time you leave an app that has One Sec applied, it re-triggers the animation, even if you’ve only had the app open for a fraction of a second, and will then notify you that “intentional app switching” is a paid feature. Essentially, the free tier is deliberately poorly designed with the express purpose of annoying and coercing its users to pay. Especially for an app like this where the developers seem fairly aware of the psychological effects possible through software design, I’m incredibly disappointed that this design choice was made. I understand having more premium features behind a paywall, but that is not what is happening here. With One Sec, after you’ve done a few minutes of work to install this app correctly, you discover that it will only actually half work unless you pay.

author: rayderlolkid

title: Instant
body: I don’t usually leave reviews, but One Sec was very quick in delivering results. I was contemplating getting what people often call a “dumb phone” to prevent wasting too much time on what modern technology enticingly presents us; after using this in conjunction with other apps like Blank Spaces, I quickly realized that all I really needed were tools like these. It allows you to personalize a good amount of how you want the app to behave. Through no fault of their own, the app has to use Apple’s Shortcuts to be able to intervene at the most important moments. Severing the dopamine hit from the action of opening certain apps certainly seems to do the trick. You’ll feel a funny frustration that makes you love the app more each time; especially if you realize that this frustration comes from the part of yourself that you so badly need to leave behind. Phenomenal app! Let’s keep supporting those who truly support us!

It all happens subconsciously. In fact, this app caused me to stop watching shorts on my iPhone and switch to watching shorts on my computer, which also happened subconsciously. I don’t really write reviews for apps, but this app turned my life around. This year I have begun to quit YouTube from my computer unless for work purposes. This app kickstarted my journey to freedom. There is a reason why this app is 4.9 stars. This app has managed to find a way to subconsciously stop people from being addicted to all sorts of apps.
